transcript.content: Hello. What brings you into the clinic today?
Hello. Lately, I feel like how my body looks and what I weigh are all I can focus on when I think about whether I’m doing well in life. It has just started to take over how I judge myself every day.
To help me understand better, have you been strictly limiting the amount of food you eat, or do you sometimes experience episodes where you feel you lose control and eat a very large amount of food?

I definitely strictly limit what I eat; I don't have times where I lose control and eat large amounts. Most days, I tell my family I already ate at work when I've really only had a coffee and half a granola bar, and at dinner I cut my portions so tiny it's barely eating. To me, it just feels like I'm finally being disciplined.
How much weight have you lost since you started restricting your food, and could you share your current height and weight?

I honestly don't know the exact amount of weight I've lost or my current numbers off the top of my head. I just know that my work pants are hanging off me now and people at the plant keep telling me I look like I'm disappearing. To me, though, it doesn't feel as extreme as everyone else makes it out to be.
Have you noticed other physical changes since losing weight, such as feeling constantly cold, dizzy, or experiencing a stop in your menstrual cycle if you have one?

To be honest, I haven't really noticed feeling unusually cold or dizzy. I also haven't paid much attention to any changes in my cycle, and I don't think those kinds of things are really happening to me.
Despite others telling you that you are disappearing, do you experience an intense fear of gaining weight or becoming fat?

Yes, I have an intense fear of gaining weight. If the scale goes up even half a pound, or if I eat something like roti or macaroni pie with my choir friends, I completely panic and feel like I’ve lost control. I immediately feel this urgent need to make up for it by cutting back even more on my food the next day.
Has a doctor or healthcare professional recently told you that your weight is dangerously low or that you are medically underweight?

Yes, my primary care doctor was very concerned about my weight loss and said my weight was too low, which is actually why she referred me here. Honestly, though, I think she and my husband are exaggerating the danger because I still have plenty of energy to work my shifts and go jogging. To me, it just feels like I'm finally being disciplined about my body.
You mentioned not paying much attention to your cycle, but looking back, have your menstrual periods stopped completely for the past three months or more?

I'm really not sure, to be honest. With all the stress of my promotion and trying to help my parents back home, I haven't kept track of my periods at all. I just haven't paid close attention to it lately.
Do you happen to remember what weight your doctor recorded at your recent visit, or could you share your height and what your typical weight used to be?
I don't remember the exact weight my doctor wrote down, and I'm not really sure of my exact height or what I used to weigh. I just know that lately all of my clothes have been hanging off me.
Even though you haven't been keeping close track, do you remember having any menstrual bleeding at all in the last three months?
I honestly don't recall. With everything going on with my promotion and my parents, I really haven't been paying attention to it at all.
Are you currently taking any birth control pills or using other hormonal contraceptives?
No, I am not currently taking any birth control pills or using other hormonal contraceptives. I haven't been on anything like that for quite some time now.
Have you noticed any other physical changes, such as your hair thinning, or the growth of fine, downy hair on your arms or face?
No, I haven't noticed any hair thinning or any fine hair growing on my arms or face. I'm really not sure about those specific physical changes, as I haven't seen anything like that happening.
Did your primary care doctor happen to mention what your BMI, or Body Mass Index, was during your recent visit?
I don't recall my doctor mentioning a specific BMI number during my visit. She only told me that she was very concerned about my weight loss and that I was too thin.
To help me understand, when is the last time you can definitely remember having a menstrual period, even if it was several months ago?
I really can't remember exactly when my last period was. It has been so long since I paid any attention to it that I honestly don't know.
Since your husband and doctor are concerned, did either of them mention how many pounds they think you have lost, or what your weight was at your last checkup?
I don't recall them mentioning an exact number of pounds or a specific weight from my checkup. Honestly, I feel like they are exaggerating the whole situation anyway, because I feel perfectly fine.
